sections.h2: Where is Rock Island County and who handles its property tax?
sections.html:
Rock Island County is on the Mississippi River in northwest Illinois, with the county seat in the city of Rock Island and the largest city, Moline, next door. It was formed in 1831 out of Jo Daviess County and named for the island in the river now called Arsenal Island. The county covers 451 square miles, about 428 of them land, and is one of the four counties in the Davenport-Moline-Rock Island metro area.

  • County Treasurer and Collector: sends the bills and takes payments at 1504 3rd Avenue, Rock Island, IL 61201.
  • Chief County Assessment Office: second floor of the same building, 309-558-3660, weekdays 8 a.m. to 4:30 p.m.
  • Township assessors: the first stop for any question about value. The county has 18 townships.
  • Board of Review: a three-member panel appointed by the County Board that hears assessment appeals.
  • County Clerk, Delinquent Tax Division: takes redemption payments, 309-558-3562.

sections.h2: What do Census figures show for Rock Island County homes?
sections.html:
QuickFacts estimates 141,869 residents for July 2025, down 1.9% from the 2020 base, in 66,873 housing units. The owner-occupied rate is 69.7%, higher than in neighboring Peoria County. The median owner-occupied value for 2020-2024 is $150,400, median gross rent is $889 and median household income is $67,159.

Retail is unusually strong for the county's size, with 2022 retail sales of $7,579,298 thousand, or $53,542 per person, which reflects shoppers crossing the river from Iowa. Transportation and warehousing receipts are $720,001 thousand. John Deere is headquartered in Moline.

The weather is cold in January, with average lows around 13 degrees Fahrenheit at Rock Island, and hot in July, with highs near 85. Interstates 74, 80, 88 and 280 cross the county, and school districts include Moline-Coal Valley, Rock Island-Milan, East Moline, Silvis and Sherrard. Median travel time to work is 19.7 minutes.

sections.h2: When are Rock Island County property taxes due?
sections.html:
Rock Island County uses four installments, which is more than many Illinois counties. The Treasurer says each installment must be paid in sequence, in full, with any penalty interest included. The 2025 taxes, payable in 2026, were due on the dates below, and the county mailed bills on or before May 1, 2026.

Rock Island County installment dates for 2025 taxes, from the County Treasurer
InstallmentDue date in 2026
FirstWednesday, June 10
SecondMonday, August 10
ThirdThursday, September 10
FourthTuesday, November 10

Those dates have passed. Expect the same four-step pattern next year, with the specific days posted by the Treasurer after the bills go out.

sections.h2: How can you pay Rock Island County property tax?
sections.html:
You can pay in six ways. Each has its own rules, and some stop before the last due date.

  • Bank or credit union: through November 10, 2026 at participating branches. Bring the whole bill with stubs, and no cards.
  • Mail: to the Rock Island County Collector, PO Box 3277, Rock Island, IL 61204-3277, postmarked on or before the due date.
  • In person: at the County Office Building. Cash, check, cashier's check and money order are taken, and cards and mobile wallets worked through November 13, 2026.
  • Drop box: in the alley and parking lot behind the County Office Building.
  • Online and phone: by e-check, card or wallet, with the phone line at 309-518-9200. The last day was November 13, 2026.
  • Autopay: online enrollment is offered.

Processing fees go to the card processor. The county lists $1.00 for an e-check and 2.45% for cards and wallets, or $2.00 on transactions under $82.00. A returned payment costs $30, and a duplicate bill costs $2. A mortgage company that wants a memo bill in place of stubs pays $5 per parcel.

sections.h2: How do assessments and appeals work in Rock Island County?
sections.html:
Township assessors value property as of January 1, the Chief County Assessment Officer reviews and equalizes the values, and the Board of Review hears complaints. After the Board of Review, a taxpayer can take an appeal to the State Property Tax Appeal Board, a five-member panel, as the county's FAQ explains.

An appeal is not a complaint about high taxes. The county's FAQ names three grounds: wrong facts on your property record card, a market value above what similar homes sold for, or a value that is accurate but higher than comparable properties. Good evidence includes a recent appraisal, nearby sales, photographs of condition, or a chart of comparable assessments.

The complaint session for 2026 has closed, and the county tells owners to speak with their township assessor about the 2027 assessment. Most normal maintenance does not raise an assessment, but a deck, a porch, an in-ground pool or a fireplace may. Taxpayers have 30 days from newspaper publication to appeal, and after the assessments are certified to the state the files are closed.

sections.h2: Which exemptions can Rock Island County owners claim?
sections.html:
The Property Tax Relief page lists many programs, and the Chief County Assessment Office will answer questions about each of them.

  • Owner-occupied: lowers equalized assessed value by up to $6,000 for owners who occupied the home on or before January 1 of the assessment year. Apply at the township assessor or the county office.
  • Senior freeze: freezes taxable assessment, not the rate. You must have owned and occupied the home on January 1 for two consecutive years, turn 65 in the assessment year, hold the senior homestead exemption and meet the income cap. The filing deadline is July 1 each year and it must be renewed annually.
  • Others: disabled persons, disabled veterans, returning veterans, natural disaster, and several charitable forms.

A new state law raised the senior freeze income limit. The county prints these maximum household incomes: $65,000 for tax year 2025, $75,000 for 2026, $77,000 for 2027 and $79,000 for 2028, after which it stays at $79,000 unless the legislature changes it.

sections.h2: What happens to unpaid Rock Island County taxes?
sections.html:
If any installment is unpaid after the last due date, the taxes enter the annual tax sale. A delinquency notice by certified mail and newspaper publication follows shortly after the fourth installment, with an added $10 fee. The county lists these costs at the sale: $94 in miscellaneous fees and $160 for canceling the sale and issuing certificates of redemption, plus interest that can run from 18% down to 0% depending on the winning bid.

Owners keep the property after the sale. They have from two and a half to three years to redeem, a period set by the tax buyer. The County Clerk takes redemption by cash, cashier's check, certified check or money order, in full at one time. Call the Delinquent Tax Division at 309-558-3562 for a quote before you plan a closing.

Escrow accounts are another trap. The county FAQ says to confirm that your mortgage company paid each installment on the right parcel, and to avoid paying twice.

faqs.q: Where do I mail a Rock Island County tax payment?
faqs.a: To the Rock Island County Collector, PO Box 3277, Rock Island, IL 61204-3277, with the payment stub. The envelope must be postmarked on or before the due date, and the county suggests alternatives because of Postal Service delays.

faqs.q: Does Rock Island County take partial tax payments?
faqs.a: No. The Treasurer does not accept partial installment payments, and installments must be paid in order. Each payment has to include any penalty interest. Delinquent taxes also have to be paid in full at one time through the County Clerk.

faqs.q: When is the Rock Island County senior freeze deadline?
faqs.a: July 1 of each year. The exemption must be renewed every year and the application goes to the Chief County Assessment Office. The county prints a household income cap that rises from $65,000 for tax year 2025 to $79,000 for 2028.

faqs.q: How long do I have to redeem sold taxes in Rock Island County?
faqs.a: From two and a half to three years from the tax sale, with the length set by the tax buyer. The County Clerk's Delinquent Tax Division at 309-558-3562 takes redemption payments in cash, cashier's check, certified check or money order.

faqs.q: What is the Rock Island County assessment office phone number?
faqs.a: The Chief County Assessment Office answers at 309-558-3660 on weekdays from 8 a.m. to 4:30 p.m. It is on the second floor of the County Office Building at 1504 Third Avenue in Rock Island.
